slides.0.title: Riesling — The King of Germany
slides.0.subtitle: The World's Greatest White Wine Grape
slides.1.title: 🍇 The Essence of Riesling
slides.1.content: Riesling is a late-ripening, high-acid white grape that originated in the Rhine region and found its most perfect terroir expression in Germany. Its thin skin makes it particularly susceptible to noble rot (Botrytis), enabling some of the world's finest sweet wines. Riesling's defining trait is its faithfulness to the soil — showing minerality on slate and floral notes on limestone — making it a true terroir variety.
slides.2.title: 🌟 Riesling's Stylistic Diversity
slides.2.items.0.text: Mosel Riesling: light (7.5–9% alcohol), powerfully mineral, with petrol and stone aromas
slides.2.items.1.text: Rheingau Riesling: medium-bodied, elegant and refined, with honey and floral notes
slides.2.items.2.text: Nahe Riesling: pronounced minerality; volcanic geology brings unique smoky character
slides.2.items.3.text: Pfalz Riesling: full-bodied (up to 13%+), tropical fruit, richly textured
slides.2.items.4.text: Rheinhessen Riesling: stylistically diverse, from crisp to richly textured
slides.3.left.items.5: GG grand cru sites: Scharzhofberg, Bernkasteler Doctor
slides.3.right.items.5: GG grand cru sites: Schloss Johannisberg, Rüdesheimer Berg
slides.4.title: ⏳ The Miracle of Aged Riesling
slides.4.content: Top Riesling shows astonishing ageing potential. Young Rieslings deliver fresh citrus and peach aromas, while with age they develop the famous 'petrol note' — a hallmark of mature Riesling. A Mosel Auslese over 10 years old reveals complex layers of honey, gingerbread and dried apricot, while TBA can age for 50+ years.
slides.5.title: 🗺️ A Panoramic Tour of Riesling Terroirs
slides.5.description: Click each of the five major regions to compare Mosel's blue slate, Rheingau's diverse soils, Pfalz's basalt, Nahe's 'soil museum' and Rheinhessen's red slopes — across soil, climate, aroma, famous Einzellagen and signature producers. The personality of one grape across very different terroirs becomes immediately clear.
slides.6.title: Quick Quiz
slides.6.questions.0.question: Which region's Riesling typically has the lowest alcohol?
slides.6.questions.0.explanation: Mosel Riesling has the lowest alcohol because of the region's high latitude and cool climate — sugar levels are lower, giving wines of just 7–9% alcohol, the lightest Riesling style in Germany.
slides.6.questions.1.question: What is the signature aroma of aged Riesling?
slides.6.questions.1.explanation: The 'petrol note' in aged Riesling is produced by the compound TDN (trimethyldihydronaphthalene). It is regarded as a hallmark of mature, top-quality Riesling — not a fault.
slides.6.questions.2.question: In the 'riesling-terroir' tour, what aromatic signature does 'Mosel blue slate' bring to Riesling?
slides.6.questions.2.options.1: Stone, smoke, high acidity and lightness
slides.6.questions.2.explanation: Blue slate reflects heat, stores warmth and contributes low-pH mineral character — giving Mosel Riesling its hallmark stone, smoke and racy acidity, alongside low alcohol (7–9%) and a featherlight body.
